title: The Road That Is Short but Long
text:
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Hananiah was one of the great sages of his generation, famous for his learning and quick wit. Yet he liked to say that only three people had ever got the better of him: a woman, a little girl and a little boy. This is the story of the boy.

He was traveling and came to a crossroads where a child was sitting. He asked the boy which road led to the city. The child pointed: this one is short and long, he said, and that one is long and short.

The rabbi, naturally, took the short road. Soon he could see the city ahead of him. But when he came close, he found that it was ringed by gardens and orchards, with walls and hedges, and there was no way through to the town. He had to turn around and walk all the way back to the crossroads.

There he found the boy again and said: my son, did you not tell me this road was short? The child answered: and did I not also tell you it was long?

Rabbi Yehoshua kissed him on the head and said: happy are you, Israel, for all of you are wise, from the greatest to the smallest.
lesson: The route that looks quickest is not always the fastest way to your actual goal. Listen to the full answer, including the part you would rather not hear.
people: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Hananiah, a child
